digest.component_or_area: S3 remote store repair / multi-bundle collapse
propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same S3 ref, git ls-remote returns ambiguous heads and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable.
git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects all push operations while bundles > 1 without writing, causing infinite retry loops because subsequent fetches cannot resolve the ambiguous ref.

The upstream Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocks on input() prompts) and discards non-chosen heads, causing permanent data loss of events unique to side-branched heads in an append-only event log.

Rebar's existing sync._do_reconverge and _union_merge already implement lossless 2-parent merges for ordinary git remotes by leveraging UUID-named event dirs that never collide and merge=ours for .bridge_state/* derived caches.

The doctor must acquire the helper's S3 per-ref lock, enumerate bundles under lock (TOCTOU guard), fetch all heads locally, merge via iterated 2-parent git merges, write the merged bundle before deleting originals, then delete N originals leaving only the merged result, ensuring ≥1 bundle with full history survives every crash point.

On unexpected non-derived-file merge conflicts, the heal aborts without deleting any remote bundle, releases locks, and surfaces fsck-recover rather than discarding a parent; concurrent doctors serialize via the helper's lock so only one merges while others back off and converge on the winner's collapsed remote.
